office.title: Indiana School Board Member
office.summary: A school board is the elected or appointed governing body of a public school corporation, the legal unit that runs a local school district {ic_20_26_5_4}{in_guide}. The board hires and evaluates the superintendent, adopts policies, and approves the annual budget, while the superintendent and staff run schools day to day {chalkbeat_2024_boards}. Most boards have five or seven members serving staggered four-year terms {chalkbeat_2024_boards}. Starting in 2026, candidates may list a political party, run as independents, or list no affiliation on the ballot, and there is no primary for these seats {in_guide}{chalkbeat_2026_primary}.

facts.label: Term
facts.value: 4 years, with elections staggered so part of the board is chosen every two years {chalkbeat_2024_boards}

facts.label: Elected
facts.value: At the November general election (November 3, 2026, or November 2028 for some seats); depending on the local organization plan, members represent the whole school corporation (at large) or a district within it, and some boards are wholly or partly appointed {in_guide}

facts.label: Ballot label
facts.value: Each candidate chooses a party label, 'Independent', or no affiliation, shown next to the name; no primary and no straight-ticket voting for these races {in_guide}{chalkbeat_2026_primary}

facts.label: Pay
facts.value: Set by board resolution: an annual amount of no more than 10% of the lowest starting teacher salary in the school corporation, plus a capped per diem {ic_20_26_4_7}

duties: Hires, evaluates and can dismiss the superintendent, and approves the hiring and firing of principals, teachers and other staff recommended by the superintendent {ic_20_26_5_4}{ic_20_26_5_4_5}{chalkbeat_2024_boards}.
Adopts the annual budget, appropriates funds and oversees school finances {ic_20_26_5_4}{chalkbeat_2024_boards}.

Decides whether to ask voters to approve an operating referendum (an extra property tax levy); the board adopts the resolution and the Department of Local Government Finance reviews the ballot language for compliance with state law {dlgf_referendum}.
Approves contracts, buys and sells property, and decides on construction, repair and demolition of school buildings {ic_20_26_5_4}.

Bargains with the teachers' union over salary, wages and wage-related benefits such as health insurance and retirement; state law excludes teacher evaluation procedures from those bargaining subjects {ic_20_29_6_4}.
Writes and updates policies and rules for schools, often in a policy handbook, including the student handbook {ic_20_26_5_4}{chalkbeat_2024_boards}.
Buys curricular materials, provides them to students without charge, and runs programs such as student transportation and school lunch {ic_20_26_5_4}.

Must adopt a process for parents and residents to ask that library material be removed as obscene or harmful to minors, review requests at public meetings and keep a public catalog of library materials {arnolt_library}.
Hears written appeals of student expulsions, unless the board has voted not to hear them {ic_20_33_8_19}.
Must take official action openly; Indiana's Open Door Law says public agencies' official action is to be conducted openly so the people may be fully informed {ic_5_14_1_5_1}{pac}.

A school board member must have lived in the school corporation (and, for a district seat, the district) for at least one year before the election, and a teacher or other employee of the school corporation may not serve on its board {in_guide}.

What the board does not control: the State Board of Education adopts statewide academic standards {ic_20_31_3_1}, the General Assembly sets the state school funding formula in the state budget {idoe_tuition}, and voucher (Choice Scholarship) eligibility is set by state law {chalkbeat_2025_budget}.
recent_changes: 2025: Senate Enrolled Act 287 allowed school board candidates to declare a party affiliation; the Indiana School Boards Association opposed the change, and a supporter quoted by WNDU, a Noblesville school board member, said it adds transparency {wndu_2026_split}.

2026: Candidates choose a party, 'Independent' or no affiliation on their nominating petition, and that choice appears on the ballot; a candidate claiming the Democratic or Republican party must have voted in that party's primary in the two most recent primaries they voted in, or have certification from the county party chair, or can be challenged and removed from the ballot {in_guide}.

July 2026: Chalkbeat reported, citing Indiana School Boards Association data, that 524 of 1,044 candidates chose a party, about 72% of them Republicans {chalkbeat_2026_takeaways}; the Indiana Election Division's 2026 guidance and the wording of the law differ on the primary-voting test, a question county election boards decide {chalkbeat_2026_ips}.

February 2026: Senate Enrolled Act 25 set the order of school board candidates on the ballot, grouped by party, with candidates who list no affiliation placed after the party and independent candidates {in_leg_2026}.

2025: Senate Enrolled Act 1, a property tax law, limits how much operating revenue districts can raise through taxes and restricts school referendums to statewide general elections in even-numbered years {chalkbeat_2025_referendums}{wfyi_2026_referendum_guide}.

2025: The same law requires districts to share operating revenue with brick-and-mortar charter schools that enroll their students, statewide starting in 2028 {chalkbeat_2025_referendums}{wfyi_2026_referendum_guide}.
2025: The state budget opened Choice Scholarship vouchers to all Indiana families starting in June 2026 {chalkbeat_2025_budget}.
2026: The Indianapolis Public Education Corporation, rather than the Indianapolis Public Schools board, now certifies Indianapolis Public Schools referendum questions for the ballot {in_leg_2026}.

2023: Senate Enrolled Act 391 changed the so-called $1 law so the Indiana Department of Education can order districts that lost at least 10% of enrollment over five years to close schools under 60% capacity and offer them to charter schools {chalkbeat_2023_dollar_law}.
2023: House Enrolled Act 1447 required school districts to set up procedures for complaints that library material is obscene or harmful to minors {arnolt_library}.
